newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX COB electricIty mostly down, PV mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX COB electricIty mostly down, PV mostly higher.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading mixed Monday in light volume that could signal the end a strong run that dominated futures trade last week, industry sources said.
"This runup has basically been based on strong daily prices, and today is the first day in a while we've seen daily prices come off," said one Houston-based futures trader.
Next-day peak Palo Verde (PV) physical power was being talked at $35.00-37.00, down from talk at $44.00-46.00 late last week for Monday delivery, the sources said.

As of 1225 EDT, June Palo Verde (PV) was bid at $25.80 and was offered at $25.95 per megawatt hour (MWh) after reaching as high as $26.10 and as low as $25.55 per MWh. The contract had last traded at $26.00, up 30 cents from Friday's settlement.
July PV was trading up 10 cents at $27.70 after hitting a new contract high of $28.10 and reaching as low as $27.40, while August PV had traded down two cents at $29.00 per MWh.

As of 1215 EDT, June California-Oregon Border (COB) futures were trading down 13 cents at $19.40 after exchanges in a range of $19.00-19.50, while July was down 15 cents at $19.85 after reaching as high as $19.90 and as low as $19.50 per MWh.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 45 COB and 138 PV contracts had traded as of 1140 EDT.

Forecasts of some cooler weather and cloud cover in the West this week were pushing short-term physical power prices lower as players looked for less cooling demand, particularily in the Southwest, the sources said.

Weather in the Southwest was expected to be three to six degrees above normal in the southern California deserts over the next several days, while thunderstorms were expected in the Arizona and New Mexico mountains keeping temperatures two to four degrees below normal.

In the Pacific Northwest, weather was expected to turn cooler in southwest Canada, Washington and Oregon over the next two days. Showers were expected through the early part of the week. The coolest temperatures were expected on Wednesday at four to six degrees below normal.

Electricity front-months hit new highs through most of last week, pushed higher by the strong physical prices, which were reported to have traded as high as $50 per MWh for next-day delivery at the Palo Verde switchyard in Arizona.
"You have to look at this as a potential top," the trader said of the mixed Monday futures activity.
As of 1220 EDT, NYMEX June Henry Hub natgas futures were down 5.9 cents at $2.19 per million British thermal units.
